evidence.audit_scope: read-only: no simulation episode, no env reset/step, no model load, no GPU; imports + file parsing only

shadow.method: git show HEAD:<path> for every libero/libero/**.py >= shadow_full (pristine complete package) and for the 4 benchmark files >= shadow_hybrid (pristine benchmark + installed LIBERO-Plus env/utils); PYTHONPATH=<shadow>; LIBERO_CONFIG_PATH=<temp config>

torch_init_load.note: pristine benchmark calls torch.load(path) without weights_only; torch 2.7.1 defaults weights_only=True and fails. The existing runtime patches torch.load(weights_only=False) at libero-runtime/tools/run_benchmark.py:50-51 before importing libero, so the pristine benchmark works under that runner. Any other harness must apply the same one-line shim.

num_steps_wait.raw: num_steps_wait: int = 10  # Number of steps to wait for objects to stabilize i n sim

num_trials_per_task.raw: num_trials_per_task: int = 50  # Number of rollouts per task

env_resolution.raw: LIBERO_ENV_RESOLUTION = 256  # resolution used to render training data

env_seed_call.raw: env.seed(seed)  # IMPORTANT: seed seems to affect object positions even when using fixed initial state

LIBERO_SPATIAL.raw: max_steps = 220  # longest training demo has 193 steps

LIBERO_OBJECT.raw: max_steps = 280  # longest training demo has 254 steps

LIBERO_GOAL.raw: max_steps = 300  # longest training demo has 270 steps

LIBERO_10.raw: max_steps = 520  # longest training demo has 505 steps

LIBERO_90.raw: max_steps = 400  # longest training demo has 373 steps

protocol_notes.eval_loop: task_suite = benchmark_dict[suite]() (task_order_index=0 => identity order for 10-task suites); env.reset(); obs=env.set_init_state(initial_states[episode_idx]); loop while t < max_steps + num_steps_wait; first num_steps_wait steps use LIBERO_DUMMY_ACTION ([0]*6+[-1]); replan every replan_steps; success when env returns done
protocol_notes.num_trials_equals_init_states: num_trials_per_task=50 == number of pruned_init states per task
